source_boundary.preserved_question_intent: Explain RocketMQ consumer message models. For the common interview meaning of consumption mode, distinguish Clustering from Broadcasting and keep this separate from Push/Pull consumer acquisition style and concurrent/orderly processing style.

sources.title: Apache RocketMQ 4.x Consumer Core Concept
anchors: RocketMQ documents two consumption modes: Clustering and Broadcasting
in Clustering, one message is processed by one consumer within the Consumer Group and consumers share the subscribed message volume
in Broadcasting, each consumer in the Consumer Group receives the full subscribed message volume
Clustering supports horizontal consumption-capacity scaling through consumers sharing work
the same document separately discusses Push and Pull as message-acquisition modes, so Push/Pull is a different classification dimension

sources.title: Apache RocketMQ 4.x Push Consumer
anchors: DefaultMQPushConsumer uses cluster mode by default
in broadcast mode every consumer in the consumer group consumes the full messages
concurrent consumption and orderly consumption are documented as a separate processing-mode distinction

sources.title: Apache RocketMQ Consumer Load Balancing
anchors: current RocketMQ documentation still distinguishes broadcast consumption from cluster consumption
cluster consumption within a consumer group uses load balancing to allocate messages to consumers
broadcast-style delivery is suitable when each subscriber needs the full stream while cluster consumption is suitable for horizontal traffic partitioning and microservice decoupling

sources.title: Apache RocketMQ Consumer Domain Model
anchors: current RocketMQ documents PushConsumer, SimpleConsumer and PullConsumer as consumer types
consumer type is a separate configuration dimension from cluster-versus-broadcast message model

claims.text: For the classic RocketMQ MessageModel/interview meaning of consumption mode, there are two modes: Clustering and Broadcasting.

In Clustering mode, consumers in the same Consumer Group share the subscribed message volume so a message is handled by one consumer in that group; this supports horizontal consumption-capacity scaling and requires load balancing/rebalancing.

In Broadcasting mode, each consumer in the Consumer Group receives the full subscribed message volume; adding consumers therefore does not divide that group's message workload in the same way as Clustering.

Push/Pull (and current PushConsumer/SimpleConsumer/PullConsumer APIs) describe how a consumer obtains messages, while concurrent/orderly describes processing behavior. These are different dimensions and must not be counted as extra Cluster/Broadcast message models.

writer_constraints: Answer the interview wording first: if consumption mode means RocketMQ MessageModel, say there are two—Clustering and Broadcasting.
Explain the unit of sharing: consumers inside one Consumer Group share work in Clustering, while each consumer receives the full subscribed stream in Broadcasting.

State the operational consequence: Clustering can scale group throughput by adding consumers up to allocation limits; Broadcasting duplicates delivery across consumers and is not a way to partition the same workload.
Keep Push/Pull or PushConsumer/SimpleConsumer/PullConsumer as a separate consumer-type/acquisition dimension, not a third/fourth cluster-broadcast mode.
Keep concurrent-versus-orderly consumption as another separate processing dimension.

Use version-sensitive wording: 4.x Java PushConsumer exposes MessageModel.CLUSTERING/BROADCASTING directly; current RocketMQ documentation still discusses cluster and broadcast consumption but consumer APIs have evolved.
Do not fabricate production throughput, lag, retry counts or company-specific usage.
